links.note: The five direct questions from Penny, Mill-wheel and Jody rewritten as reported questions are 31622 exactly.
Fifteen sentences from the lesson sorted by asking a what/who question of the verb is 31623.
The ten lesson words put in dictionary order with their idioms and phrasal verbs is 31624.

Whether it is right to kill an animal to save a human life is the doe's killing in 31608, whose heart and liver drew out the rattlesnake poison. 31611 is the obligation that killing created, which 92268 tests.
Persuading unwilling parents to let you keep an animal is the argument of 31609, which leaves Penny no answer and hems him in. 31612 is the mother's condition once she has agreed.
What we owe nature for what we take from it is Doc Wilson's ruling in 31611 - nothing in the world comes quite free, and the life Penny keeps was paid for. 31608 is the killing itself.
The home remedy for the snakebite is the doe's liver in 31608; the item asks what should be done instead today.
He put it to his father first, and 31609 is that request and its argument. 31610 is the later approach to his mother.
The praise for keeping his head in an emergency is 31607 word for word.
'Hungry and very scared' is part of the plea that hems Penny in, 31609. 31615 is what he actually finds at the clearing.
'Ungrateful to leave it to starve' is the third limb of the argument summarised in 31609.
His mother stopped with the coffee pot held in mid-air - 31610, which is her whole reaction. 31612 is her consent afterwards.
That he did not want company is 31614, with its two reasons - the disappointment he could not bear to have seen, and a meeting too secret to share.
The tall pine that guided him belongs to the trek that ends at the clearing of 31615; no concept in this set covers the walk separately.
Throwing the bough at the buzzards is part of the clearing scene, 31615.
The buzzards clacking their wings and returning to the carcass is inside 31615. 31616 begins once he has found the fawn.

'The touch made him delirious' sits in the stroking passage of 31617; 'delirious' is not one of the ten dictionary words of 31624, so the item is anchored to its beat rather than to the language exercise.
'Light-headed' is a meaning question on 'light', one of the ten words 31624 has learners look up with their idioms. Not 31617, because what is tested is the word, not the moment.
Penny's gladness comes when the fawn is carried in to him, which is 31619. 31607 is his earlier praise of the boy.
The tongue against his hand is the feeding by fingers held under the milk, 31621. 31620 is the failed attempt with the gourd just before it.
